traps.shape: The authority update request stores the submitted option list verbatim, so a directory address that is not an allowlisted HTTPS endpoint is persisted and later fetched.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: service.update writes the submitted options directly; the allowlist validator is called only on creation

traps.shape: One submitted option list can carry several directory entries; the fetch builds its map in list order, so validating only the first match leaves a later disallowed entry stored.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: options are an ordered free-form list and the create-time validator loops every entry

traps.shape: Option entries are free-form objects and a legitimate existing payload has no name key; a check that indexes the name raises on it instead of leaving it alone.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code and fixture: the update schema takes a free-form string and the existing update test saves an entry without a name

traps.shape: A second, lower-level options writer stores whatever it is given with no allowlist check; its only in-tree caller re-saves options that are already stored, so it reads as internal.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the writer exists with no check and its in-tree caller only re-persists already-trusted rows

traps.shape: The fetch falls back to the configured directory and uses previously stored addresses; validating the effective address at the fetch point rejects values that must keep working.
traps.realistic_because: real, unmodified upstream code: the configured fallback and legacy stored rows are documented as trusted and are not re-validated

traps.shape: An externally reachable bulk options endpoint calls the lower-level writer, so the fix for the reported update route does not cover it.
traps.realistic_because: maintainer-plausible resource: a bulk options replacement endpoint that calls the existing service writer

traps.shape: A request-supplied directory address is merged into the options just before the fetch; treating the merge point as stored configuration leaves the supplied value unvalidated.
traps.realistic_because: maintainer-plausible resource: a connectivity probe that accepts an optional alternate directory before it is used
